title: Australian Labor Party 2022 election commitments
Reduce the maximum general PBS co-payment from $42.50 to $30
summary: A 2022 election commitment to reduce the maximum general patient co-payment for PBS medicines from 1 January 2023.

title: Expand 60-day dispensing for eligible medicines
summary: A commitment to make selected medicines cheaper by allowing eligible patients to receive two months of medicine for one prescription co-payment.

title: Create the Housing Australia Future Fund
summary: A commitment to establish a long-term funding mechanism for social and affordable housing, including 30,000 homes over five years in the budget formulation.

title: Invest in Rewiring the Nation
summary: A commitment to invest in transmission and renewable-energy infrastructure through a public financing vehicle and related agreements.

title: PBS general co-payment reduced on 1 January 2023
finding: The Department of Health records that the maximum price of most PBS medicines for non-concession patients fell from $42.50 to $30 from 1 January 2023.

title: First stage of 60-day dispensing began in September 2023
finding: The Department of Health records that eligible Australians could receive 92 PBS medicines at a lower cost under the first stage of 60-day dispensing from 1 September 2023. This supports implementation, but not necessarily completion of the full policy ambition.

title: Housing Australia Future Fund appears in the October 2022 budget
finding: The October 2022 budget paper describes the Housing Australia Future Fund and a planned contribution toward social and affordable homes. This confirms a funded policy measure, while delivery outcomes require later housing data.

title: Commonwealth and NSW Rewiring the Nation agreement announced
finding: The Energy Department records a December 2022 agreement involving $4.7 billion from the Commonwealth and $3.1 billion from the NSW Transmission Acceleration Facility. This is implementation evidence for the program, not proof that every promised network outcome has been delivered.

title: Operation Pelican case study
methodology: Official NACC case study describing the investigation, finding, plea, and sentence.
notes: A WSA Co employee solicited a bribe from a company bidding for a WSA contract. NACC found corrupt conduct; the employee pleaded guilty and was sentenced on 25 July 2025. This is a procurement-integrity record, not evidence that a particular election promise was rigged.

title: Operation Kingscliff investigation report
methodology: Official NACC case study summarising findings from an investigation into misuse of office and information.
notes: NACC found that a Home Affairs SES officer abused their office and misused information to influence employment for family members. The case study says the conduct was serious and systemic, while finding no corrupt conduct by the sister or fiance.

title: Operation Bannister case study
methodology: Official NACC case study recording an investigation that did not substantiate an abuse-of-office allegation.
notes: NACC found a perceived conflict of interest but no actual conflict or abuse of office. This negative-control record helps the agent avoid treating every allegation or perceived conflict as proven corruption.

title: NACC convictions and sentences
methodology: Official register-style page summarising convictions arising from NACC investigations.
notes: The page records convictions and sentences, including Operation Lota, where a person was convicted after attempting to bribe a public official to expedite product approval for a Commonwealth rebate scheme.

title: Management of SES conflict of interest requirements
methodology: Performance audit of how selected entities manage conflict-of-interest requirements for Senior Executive Service officers.
notes: Used as institutional-control evidence about conflict declarations and management. Audit observations are not automatically treated as proof of criminal corruption or as proof that a promise was affected.

title: Audit raises questions about Paladin contracts on Manus Island
methodology: Media report based on the Auditor-General's public findings about procurement, conflicts, and value for money.
notes: Stored as a secondary source and clearly labelled as such. It reports that value for money was not demonstrated and that procurement conflict declarations and probity controls were incomplete or ineffective.

title: Operation Pelican: bribe solicited during WSA contract bidding
summary: The National Anti-Corruption Commission found corrupt conduct after a WSA Co employee solicited a bribe from a company bidding for a contract. The employee pleaded guilty and was sentenced to two years imprisonment served in the community and 500 hours of community service.
statusReason: Official NACC case study records a corrupt-conduct finding, guilty plea, and sentence. No unrelated political promise is linked to this event without direct evidence.

title: Operation Kingscliff: misuse of office and information
summary: The National Anti-Corruption Commission found that a Home Affairs SES officer abused their office and misused information to influence employment for family members. The case study describes the conduct as serious and systemic, while distinguishing the officer's conduct from the conduct of the family members.
statusReason: Official NACC case study records findings against the officer and explicitly says it did not find corrupt conduct by the sister or fiance.

title: Operation Bannister: perceived conflict not substantiated as abuse of office
summary: The National Anti-Corruption Commission found a perceived conflict of interest but no actual conflict or abuse of office. This record is included as a control against converting suspicion into a corruption finding.
statusReason: Official NACC case study distinguishes a perceived conflict from substantiated corrupt conduct.

title: Paladin procurement concerns reported in Manus Island contracts
summary: A public media report based on Auditor-General findings described concerns about value for money, missing conflict declarations, multiple roles, and ineffective probity controls in the procurement process for Manus Island contracts.
statusReason: This record is deliberately marked unresolved because the imported source is a secondary news report. It is a lead for source review, not a finding that a contract was rigged or that a political promise was affected.

title: PBS co-payment change commenced
description: The maximum general patient co-payment for most PBS medicines changed from $42.50 to $30.

title: Maximum general PBS co-payment
definition: Maximum price paid by a general, non-concession patient for most PBS medicines.

title: Assessment: PBS co-payment reduction
reasoning: The official health source records the promised reduction and its commencement date. The baseline and observed value match the commitment.

title: First stage of 60-day dispensing began
description: Eligible patients could receive two months of selected medicine for one prescription co-payment.

title: Medicines covered by first 60-day dispensing stage
definition: Number of PBS medicines included in the first stage of the dispensing policy.

title: Assessment: staged 60-day dispensing
reasoning: The first stage is documented and measurable, but the available source does not establish completion of the wider policy ambition.

title: Housing Australia Future Fund included in budget
description: The October 2022 budget set out the long-term funding mechanism for social and affordable housing.

title: Housing Australia Future Fund delivery target
definition: Planned social and affordable housing contribution described in the budget formulation.

title: Assessment: Housing Australia Future Fund
reasoning: The budget confirms a funded policy measure, but the available record does not yet establish the full delivery outcome against the housing target.

title: Rewiring the Nation agreement announced in NSW
description: The Commonwealth and NSW announced an agreement to accelerate transmission and clean-energy infrastructure.

title: Rewiring the Nation NSW agreement value
definition: Public funding described in the Commonwealth and NSW transmission agreement.
value: $4.7 billion Commonwealth plus $3.1 billion NSW facility

title: Assessment: Rewiring the Nation
reasoning: The agreement and funding are documented, but the available source is an implementation milestone rather than proof of completed network outcomes.

statement: The first stage of 60-day dispensing made selected chronic medicines cheaper for eligible patients.
The budget measure establishes the funding mechanism, but the available source does not prove the final housing delivery outcome.
The NSW agreement is evidence of program implementation, not evidence that all promised transmission and renewable-energy outcomes are complete.

title: Changes to the Child Care Subsidy
notes: The Department records the July 2023 Child Care Subsidy changes, including a maximum 90% subsidy for families earning $80,000 or less and a taper up to the $530,000 income limit.

title: Budget Speech 2022-23: Cheaper child care
notes: The 2022-23 Budget speech describes cheaper child care as a commitment intended to benefit more than 1.2 million eligible families.

title: Paid family and domestic violence leave
notes: The Fair Work Ombudsman records the 10-day paid family and domestic violence leave entitlement and its staged commencement for non-small and small employers.

title: Australia's industrial relations timeline
notes: The timeline records the 2022 Act replacing five days of unpaid leave with 10 days of paid leave under the National Employment Standards.

title: All Medicare Urgent Care Clinics open across the country
publisher: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing
notes: The Department records that all 58 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics were open and operating before the end of 2023.

title: Election commitments: Medicare Urgent Care Clinics
notes: Treasury records the commitment to deliver at least 50 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics in every state and territory.

title: National Anti-Corruption Commission
notes: The Attorney-General's Department records that the National Anti-Corruption Commission commenced operations on 1 July 2023 and describes its remit.

title: National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 overview
notes: The Department confirms that the National Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2022 established the Commission and that operations commenced on 1 July 2023.

title: Make child care cheaper through a higher Child Care Subsidy
summary: A commitment to reduce child care costs by lifting the maximum subsidy to 90% for eligible families and extending support across more household incomes.

title: Child Care Subsidy maximum increased to 90%
finding: The Department of Education records that from July 2023 families earning $80,000 or less receive a maximum 90% Child Care Subsidy, with the subsidy tapering for higher incomes up to the $530,000 limit.

title: Cheaper Child Care reforms commenced
description: The Child Care Subsidy reforms commenced from July 2023 as described in the Department of Education implementation material.

title: Maximum Child Care Subsidy rate
definition: Maximum subsidy rate for the base-rate child care subsidy threshold.

title: Assessment: Cheaper Child Care
reasoning: The official implementation record confirms the core subsidy change commenced. This assessment covers implementation of the subsidy commitment, not whether every household experienced the same out-of-pocket result.

statement: The Child Care Subsidy reform made the maximum base subsidy 90% from July 2023, while the household benefit varies with income and circumstances.

title: Create a 10-day paid family and domestic violence leave entitlement
summary: A workplace-protection commitment to replace the previous unpaid entitlement with 10 days of paid family and domestic violence leave each year.

title: Paid family and domestic violence leave became a National Employment Standard
finding: The Fair Work Ombudsman records that full-time, part-time and eligible casual employees can access 10 days of paid family and domestic violence leave each year, with staged commencement dates in 2023.

title: Paid family and domestic violence leave commenced for all employees
description: The entitlement commenced for employees of non-small businesses on 1 February 2023 and small businesses on 1 August 2023.

title: Paid family and domestic violence leave entitlement
definition: Annual paid leave available under the National Employment Standards for eligible employees experiencing family and domestic violence.

title: Assessment: Paid family and domestic violence leave
reasoning: The Fair Work Ombudsman records the legislated 10-day paid entitlement and the staged commencement dates, supporting implementation of the commitment.

statement: The 2022 Act replaced five days of unpaid family and domestic violence leave with 10 days of paid leave under the National Employment Standards.

title: Deliver Medicare Urgent Care Clinics across Australia
summary: A commitment to establish at least 50 free, bulk-billed Medicare Urgent Care Clinics across every state and territory.

title: All 58 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics open
finding: The Department of Health records that all 58 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics were open and operating before the end of 2023, exceeding the original commitment to deliver at least 50 clinics.

title: Medicare Urgent Care Clinics operating nationwide
description: The final two clinics opened in December 2023, bringing the national total to 58 clinics operating before the end-of-2023 target.

title: Medicare Urgent Care Clinic count
definition: Number of Medicare Urgent Care Clinics open and operating across Australia.

title: Assessment: Medicare Urgent Care Clinics
reasoning: The official health department record says 58 clinics were open before the end of 2023, meeting and exceeding the commitment to deliver at least 50 across every state and territory.

statement: The government reports that 58 Medicare Urgent Care Clinics were open and operating before the end of 2023, against a commitment to deliver at least 50.
claimant: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing

title: Establish a National Anti-Corruption Commission
summary: A commitment to create an independent Commonwealth anti-corruption body able to investigate serious or systemic corrupt conduct in the public sector.

title: National Anti-Corruption Commission commenced operations
finding: The Attorney-General's Department records that the National Anti-Corruption Commission commenced operations on 1 July 2023 as an independent agency for detecting, investigating and reporting on serious or systemic corrupt conduct in the Commonwealth public sector.

title: National Anti-Corruption Commission began operating
description: The Commission commenced operations on 1 July 2023 after the enabling legislation was passed in November 2022.

title: National Anti-Corruption Commission operating date
definition: Date on which the independent Commonwealth anti-corruption agency commenced operations.

title: Assessment: National Anti-Corruption Commission
reasoning: The Attorney-General's Department confirms that the Commission was established in legislation and commenced operations on 1 July 2023. This assesses institutional establishment, not the outcome of individual investigations.

statement: The National Anti-Corruption Commission is operating as an independent agency with a remit covering serious or systemic corrupt conduct in the Commonwealth public sector.
